name: LGD-2941

lead: LGD-2941 (also LGD-122941) is a nonsteroidal SARM of the quinolinone class, explored for muscle wasting, low testosterone and bone loss. Muscle-building communities treat it as a lean mass candidate.

Like other SARMs, it is designed to activate the androgen receptor selectively in muscle and bone, the chain being anabolic signalling in muscle and more lean mass. Its development has reportedly stopped after a Phase I trial was discontinued. Very little is published beyond its chemistry, and no human results were identified.

paras: There is little community material and no established routine for appearance use.
No safety data are public. It is unapproved, and SARMs generally are banned in sport.

angle.text: LGD-2941 is a quinolinone SARM that muscle-building communities treat as a lean mass candidate, designed to activate the androgen receptor selectively in muscle. It was investigated for cachexia and hypogonadism, then discontinued after Phase I.

lead: LGD-2941 (also LGD-122941) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the quinolinone class that was investigated for cachexia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis [1][2]. Wikipedia reports that it is no longer being developed, and its Phase I trial was discontinued [1][2].

Very little published information exists beyond its chemistry; a 2008 paper on related oxazinoquinolinone SARMs is the main cited literature [1]. It is not about appearance enhancement per se, and no community material or human results were identified.

paras: It is a quinolinone derivative bearing a pyrrolidine ring and trifluoromethyl groups, with a molar mass of about 394 g/mol [1].
No studies found. A Phase I trial is reported to have been discontinued, and no results were identified [2].

Wikipedia lists it among abandoned drugs and states that development has ended, citing a pharmaceutical database [1]. SARMs as a class are unapproved by the FDA and EMA and are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency [2].
